proof_checks: Argument reconstruction: For any finite rooted tree, deleting leaf h of M moves its charge to parent g via P_ME. The residual is D x_M = q(δ_h - δ_g) with q = x_M(h). Inclusion I_MX embeds this into X. Projection P_XV to V yields q(δ_h - δ_g) if h ∈ V (since g ∈ V by ancestor closure), and 0 otherwise (since h and g map to the same retained ancestor). This confirms the exact set of nonzero holders is {V : h ∈ V} for q ≠ 0.
Unit-conductance Green step: The potential f(z) = q * 1[h is an ancestor of z] on V has Laplacian q at h and -q at g, exactly matching P_XV d. This confirms the exact response step.
Old-amplitude recovery: Depends exactly on overlap source compatibility. For J = M ∩ V, h is a leaf of J. Thus q = P_MJ x_M(h) = P_VJ x_V(h), which is the sum of x_V(z) over V-descendants of h.
Passive invariance: Depends exactly on coverage preservation (union U is unchanged) and initial compatible response classes. By O2-O4, the glued source and response on U remain identical.

Mean-centering vs gauge: Adding a constant to a potential is a gauge change, but a unit balanced source dipole changes the physical drop. Independent mean-centering fails because pushing (1,1,1) on o-h-w to (o,h) gives (1,2); local mean-centering gives a drop of 1/2, whereas global gives 0.

Bounded enumeration: check_loss_support.py successfully tests h internal to X but a leaf of M, proper union, multiple holders, signed cancellation, and nonzero negative q (-2). Rational column checks confirm the matrix identities.
